record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: How can the federated-learning community develop new datasets that better represent real-world federated problems, including unbalanced and non-IID client partitions, scale-sensitive cross-device scenarios, metadata such as timestamps or geolocation, and feature-partitioned cross-silo datasets?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Design a methodology for constructing benchmark datasets for federated learning that faithfully reflect realistic deployment conditions. A federated learning setting consists of a (possibly very large) collection of clients $\{C_i\}_{i\in I}$, each holding a local dataset $D_i$ drawn from a client-specific distribution $P_i$ over a feature-label space $\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$. Construct a family of benchmark datasets satisfying all of the following properties simultaneously:

1. (Unbalanced partitions) The sizes $|D_i|$ follow a heavy-tailed distribution across clients, reflecting real-world participation imbalance.
2. (Non-IID partitions) The local distributions $P_i$ differ across clients in label distribution, feature distribution, and/or conditional distribution $P_i(y\mid x)$, in ways quantifiably similar to those observed in real federated deployments.
3. (Cross-device scale sensitivity) The benchmark supports the cross-device regime, with $|I|$ on the order of $10^6$ or more clients, each holding a small $D_i$, and includes mechanisms to evaluate algorithms whose behavior is sensitive to the total number of participating clients.
4. (Metadata) Each example or each client carries auxiliary metadata such as timestamps and geolocation tags, enabling study of temporal drift, non-stationarity, and spatial heterogeneity.
5. (Feature-partitioned cross-silo data) The benchmark includes a vertical federated learning variant in which a fixed set of entities is described by disjoint feature subsets $\mathcal{X}=\mathcal{X}_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal{X}_k$ held by distinct silos, with consistent entity-linking information.

Provide rigorous criteria (e.g., quantitative measures of non-IIDness, imbalance, and drift) under which a proposed dataset family is declared representative of real-world federated problems, and exhibit such a dataset family meeting these criteria.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an open research direction in federated learning. While several benchmark suites (LEAF, FedScale, FLamby, TFF datasets) have partially addressed unbalanced, non-IID, and cross-device settings, no single benchmark family is widely accepted as covering all listed properties (scale, metadata such as timestamps/geolocation, and vertical/feature-partitioned cross-silo data) with rigorous representativeness criteria. The problem remains open as a community goal.

status_evidence.title: FedScale: Benchmarking Model and System Performance of Federated Learning at Scale
status_evidence.snippet: FedScale provides realistic datasets at large scale for cross-device FL benchmarking.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress toward scale-sensitive cross-device benchmarks exists, but coverage of all desiderata is incomplete.

status_evidence.title: LEAF: A Benchmark for Federated Settings
status_evidence.snippet: LEAF provides federated datasets with natural non-IID partitions.
status_evidence.claim: Existing benchmarks address some but not all of the listed properties.

status_evidence.title: FLamby: Datasets and Benchmarks for Cross-Silo Federated Learning in Healthcare
status_evidence.snippet: Cross-silo benchmarks in healthcare; does not cover vertical FL broadly.
